title.narrative: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Integrated Tourism Development Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Integrated Tourism Development Project for Pakistan is to improve tourism-enabling infrastructure, enhance tourism assets, and strengthen destination management for sustainable tourism development in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The project comprises of four components. The first component, sector enablement and tourism entrepreneurship aims to strengthen and formalize Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's travel and tourism (T and T) sector. The second component, infrastructure planning and development will support the provincial government with the planning and development of the public infrastructure, while identifying the opportunities for mobilizing private sector investments. The third component, project management and capacity building will support the following activities: (a) supporting project management and capacity building; (b) implementing environmental preservation and waste management activities; and (c) carrying out civil works for the appropriate functioning of Project Management Unit - Department of Culture, Sports, Tourism, and Youth Affairs (PMU-DoT) and PMU - Communication and Works Department (C and W). The fourth component, contingent emergency response component will provide immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.

The project development objective is to improve tourism-enabling infrastructure, enhance tourism assets, and strengthen destination management for sustainable tourism development in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

condition.narrative: The Project Implementing Entity shall ensure that DoT and C&W will maintain their respective Project Management Units withcomposition and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, to carry out the day-to-day implementation of the activitiesunder their respective parts of the Project (including compliance with the Safeguards Instruments) throughout projectimplementation.
The Project Implementing Entity shall maintain, throughout Project implementation, and publicize the availability of a grievancemechanism, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

The Project Implementing Entity shall, no later than one month after the Effective Date, appoint and thereafter maintain throughthe period of implementation of the Project, (i) a full-time Project director with full administrative and financial powers, eachfor PMU-DoT and for PMU-C&W, for the sanctioning of expenditures and approval of payments, and (ii) a finance manager, each forPMU-DoT and for PMU-C&W, all with terms of reference satisfactory to the Association.

The Project Implementing Entity shall, no later than one month after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintainthroughout the period of implementation of the Project, a Project Steering Committee, with composition and terms of referencesatisfactory to the Association.

The Project Implementing Entity shall, no later than three months after the Effective Date, prepare and adopt a Project OperationsManual, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association and carry out the Project in accordance with the POM.

The Recipient shall ensure, and cause the Project Implementing Entity to ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance withthe Safeguards Instruments (ESMF, Sub-project ESMP, Sub-project ESIA, IPPF, Sub-Project IPP, RPF, Sub-project RAP, PhysicalCulturalResource Management Framework, Physical Cultural Resource Management Plan).

The Recipient shall ensure, and cause the Project Implementing Entity to ensure, that all civil works under the Project include theobligation of contractors, subcontractors and supervising entities to comply with the relevant aspects of Safeguard Instruments.

The ITZ feasibilities and DIMPs are expected to mobilize and capture pipeline investments during FY25 (Q4). The GoKP received US$350,000 as lease amount for the PTDC properties using the project completed Asset Valuation Study.

title.narrative: Improved Planning and Management of Tourist Destinations.

comment.narrative:
1. Master Plan for the four Integrated Tourism Zones (ITZs) were completed and disseminated at the Dubai Expo (Mar 2022). The first Investment Readiness Conference for ITZs was held in 2022 in Karachi.
2. The Destination Investment and Management Plans (DIMPs) for Upper Swat, Kumrat and Chitral were launched in Dec 2022.
3. Asset Valuation Analysis was carried out for the 19 properties handed over by the Pakistan Tourism Development Corporation (PTDC) to GoKP. These properties were transferred to a public limited company to mobilize investors.
4. The Conservation and Management Plan for the Peshawar Musuem was completed in 2023.

title.narrative: Public sector professionals receive training in Tourism and Project Management.

comment.narrative:
1. Training were held at Swat, Chitral, Abbottabad, Mansehra, and Peshawar on Solid Waste Management and sustainable tourism that were attended by 201 persons including 40 women from public sector.
2. Hospitality Training Program jointly organized by the Serena Hotels and Ecole Switzerland was attended by 5 persons from public sector including one female official.
3. Public sector representatives participated in the workshop on ITZs (51 participants including 5 women), DIMPs (60 participants including 6 women), and public private partnership (40 participants including 10 women).
The numbers were reported twice for two indicators and being fixed in this ISR to address double counting.

title.narrative: Digital Data Collection and Monitoring System for T&T sector established.

comment.narrative: The e-booking system for tourists was piloted in Aug 2021 by DoT. A Tourism Management Information System (TMIS) was developed and will be launched in Feb 2025. The Tourist Facilitation Hub (TFH) developed through KITE collects periodic data on tourist traffic, weather, tourist feedback and relevant stats in coordination with the relevant departments and private sector. These updates are disseminated through social media to keep the visitors informed.
